title: Disentangled Relational Graph Neural Network with Contrastive Learning for Knowledge Graph Completion

items.abstract: <jats:p>Emotion Recognition in Conversation (ERC) is a key task in human-computer interaction and affective computing. Currently, leveraging graph neural networks to model the complex interactions among speakers has become mainstream. However, existing methods still face three major challenges: first, it is difficult to effectively filter out emotion-irrelevant noise during feature extraction; second, the intra-modal and inter-modal dependencies are coupled within a single graph structure, limiting the model&apos;s fine-grained modeling capability; third, static graph construction often introduces a large number of noisy connections, which interfere with information propagation between nodes. To address these issues, we propose a multi-graph heterogeneous graph neural network based on reinforcement learning and a decoupled contrastive loss function (RL-DCLHGNN). First, a decoupled contrastive loss function is designed in the upstream task, which separates task-relevant features from irrelevant ones by pulling positive sample pairs closer in the task-relevant feature space while pushing them away from negative samples. Second, a heterogeneous graph structure that separates intra-modal and inter-modal relationships is constructed to capture different levels of interactions respectively. Finally, reinforcement learning technology is introduced into the node connection strategy, and a dynamic sliding window mechanism is designed, enabling the model to adaptively adjust the number of connected nodes based on the current dialogue context. Extensive experiments on the IEMOCAP and MELD datasets demonstrate that RL-DCLHGNN achieves superior performance.</jats:p>
title: Multi-graph Decoupled Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network with Reinforcement Learning and Decoupled Contrastive Loss

title: CL-GNN: Contrastive Learning and Graph Neural Network for ProteinLigand Binding Affinity Prediction

items.abstract: <jats:p>As digital data volumes surge, recommendation systems have emerged as a vital solution to mitigate information overload. Traditional methods such as collaborative filtering and content-based filtering serve as the foundation of this field. However, these systems—particularly collaborative filtering—face major challenges such as data sparsity and over-smoothing. Recent advancements in deep learning, specifically Graph Neural Network (GNN) models like LightGCN, have proven effective in capturing complex structural user-item relationships. The proposed model integrates Contrastive Learning as an additional supervision mechanism to address overfitting issue that usually appear when model occurs data sparsity. This mechanism enables the model to learn more robust latent features through self-supervised learning while preventing representation degradation in deep graph layers. Furthermore, temporal contexts—including day, month, hour, season, year, and weekend status—are incorporated to capture dynamic user preferences more accurately. Experiments conducted in an offline environment using the MovieLens 1M dataset yielded significant results. The model integrating LightGCN, Contrastive Learning, and temporal context successfully achieved a Hit Ratio of 70.74%. Additionally, the model recorded an NDCG of 0.1888, an MRR of 0.3383, Recall@20 of 0.0628, and a MAP of 0.0959. The proposed model also demonstrated a 4.62% improvement in Hit Ratio compared to the baseline model.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Motivation. Microbial communities, including bacteria, archaea, viruses, protozoa and fungi, interact with drugs through metabolism, detoxification, resistance and therapeutic response. Experimental screening of drug-microbe associations is slow and costly while computational prediction of pairs can support drug repurposing, antimicrobial discovery and precision medicine. Many models of graph neural network (GNN) represent drugs and microbes with similarities, such as Gaussian interaction profile (GIP) kernels, computed from the drug-microbe interaction matrix. Since these similarities are derived from the same associations being predicted, their random-split evaluation would be sensitive to the feature-construction protocol. This motivates the models that rely on chemical and biological covariates and evaluations that state clearly which information is available to the models.,Results. We introduce a novel GNN that leverages contrastive learning to predict drug-microbe associations. Our approach is built upon a multi-view representation strategy, wherein each drug is characterized by three complementary chemical modalities and each microbe is encoded through three distinct biological views. This heterogeneous feature fusion enables the model to capture complex interactional patterns from diverse biomedical data sources. The model comprises three parallel branches, each corresponding to a distinct view pair that combines one drug view with one microbe view. Within each branch, we construct a heterogeneous graph, in which drug-drug and microbe-microbe edges are defined by similarity scores, while drug-microbe edges are derived exclusively from the known training associations. Every branch processes its graph through a dedicated graph convolutional network (GCN). Subsequently, a link predictor is applied to score candidate drug-microbe pairs, and a projection head is employed to align the learned representations across branches, ensuring consistency among the complementary views. We evaluate our model using fivefold crossvalidation (5-CV) on a complete set of experimentally verified drug-microbe associations in three publicly available benchmark datasets: MDAD, aBiofilm, and DrugVirus. To ensure unbiased assessment, we employ a dedicated evaluation split, which was withheld from training and previously used solely for viewpair selection. Moreover, we evaluate our model on an independent hold-out test set and on an external database, and present case studies. Our model achieves strong performance across all datasets, with AUC/AUPR scores of 0.940/0.948 on MDAD, 0.926/0.931 on aBiofilm, and 0.878/0.870 on DrugVirus. In a complementary analysis, we investigate the impact of incorporating GIP features under a standard randomsplit evaluation protocol. While the inclusion of GIP features improves predictive accuracy, we emphasize that this improvement reflects a protocolsensitivity effect rather than a corrected or enhanced performance estimate for our model or prior work.</jats:p>
title: Drug-microbe association prediction using graph neural network with triple-view contrastive learning
